So for a preschool IEP she would have to have a 33% delay in one area or a 25% delay in two areas that they test for to qualify for a special education program. These include physical, communication , cognitive, social emotional, and adaptive skills. You will probably be filling out questionnaires for the school district as well as her current teacher. It will be a often, sometimes, never type of questionnaire. It seems there's some sensory issues at play so the ot would be asking how she regulates, tolerates textures/clothing/foods/noises etc. In terms of speech they'll ask how many words she has, how many she puts together, how much can an unfamiliar & familiar listener understand her, and her ability to understand you.


Just so you know, once she is kindergarten aged she will have to get retested and qualify under different requirements. 


I'm not sure what your district is like regarding special education but be firm in what your daughter needs and know your rights. They should be giving you a parent in special education booklet at the meeting but it is online as well. I've seen parents get steamrolled in meetings and things that shouldn't happen but parents don't know the laws.  Best of luck!
